f3_caveats: Only `interpret`, `plan` and `coder` are connected to the gateway; every other node stays deterministic
The real-provider test is opt-in and was NOT executed: no credentials in the environment (see technical_debt TD-01)
AI_SWE_MODEL_PRICING is empty in the repository, so cost is None (unknown), never 0
The pricing table has a loading mechanism but no tariff is asserted as current
No authentication yet (open finding from the external audit)
f4_caveats: RunPlan is the contract that bounds the plan: DFS cycle detection, unique ids, existing dependencies, <=32 subtasks, agent != supervisor, non-empty allowed_tools
max_review_cycles is clamped to the run budget when the model asks for more; the clamp is declared in the rationale
Topology edges are static: a plan -circular or gigantic- can never introduce a loop in the execution
The deterministic fallback is declared with a recoverable MODEL_FALLBACK error, never silent
f5_caveats: Execution is now subtask-by-subtask via plan_index; the router reads the index and sends to the next agent
Evidence accumulates immutably: each researcher execution concatenates findings to the previous ones
All executor nodes (researcher, coder) advance plan_index by 1; the router only compares, never calculates
The plan is consumed sequentially; dependencies (depends_on) are NOT yet respected before execution (F6)
When the plan is exhausted, execution goes to finalize regardless of intent (the plan is the source of truth)
f6_caveats: The model generates a CodeProposal (path, operation, new_content, rationale); it never generates a CodeChange
The system -not the model- derives the unified diff, the added/removed line counts and every sha256: a model cannot know the hash of a file it has not written
FileOperation (create/modify/delete) exists because a deleted file with added=0/removed=N is indistinguishable from a modified one
The unified diff is line-level and has no old content: `create` treats the previous file as empty, `delete` as fully removed. F7 (sandbox) is what will hold both versions
Scope limits (max_files_changed, max_lines_changed) are enforced by trimming and the trim is declared with a SCOPE_TRIMMED error, never silent
The fallback is a controlled EMPTY change plus a recoverable MODEL_FALLBACK error: no invented patch, ever
The Coder consumes budget and writes NOTHING to disk; applying the patch is F7
ProjectRequirements does not exist (NOT_IMPLEMENTED per the F2 audit): the Coder works from TaskInterpretation, Evidence and the current Subtask
f7_caveats: The sandbox is a real `git worktree` per run, created detached at HEAD under workspace_root (var/workspaces/<run_id>), which is gitignored: the original repo never sees the changes
The sandbox requires a real git repository and a commit: `git worktree add` cannot work without a HEAD

Confinement is four barriers per write: normalize_rel_path (syntax) + path_within_scope (declared scope) + Policy Engine decide() (role/subtask/protection/budget) + the physical check that the resolved path stays inside the sandbox root
A blocked path is a DENIAL, not a fault: it is recorded in `denegados` and the rest of the change still applies - one malicious file does not abort a legitimate change

The unified diff is now real (difflib, old vs new content) when the sandbox supplies the previous content; without it the diff still degrades to the F6 whole-file form and the `/dev/null` header declares it
`git diff HEAD` does not see untracked files: the sandbox runs `git add -N` first, otherwise a `create` would report an empty diff
The Coder CANNOT delete: `delete_file` is Supervisor-only and approval-gated, so a proposed `delete` is denied by policy and the file survives in the sandbox
The sandbox is NOT yet wired into the graph: F7 provides the mechanism (create/apply/teardown) plus tests; promotion of changes to the user repo is not implemented

The fourth barrier (physical root check) is covered by a test that INJECTS the resolution for the destination path, because the canonical attack vector - a symlink inside the worktree pointing outside - cannot be constructed on this Windows machine: `os.symlink` for directories creates a link that neither `Path.resolve()` nor `os.path.realpath()` follows, so resolution never leaves the root and the barrier has nothing to judge. `test_la_plataforma_no_permite_construir_el_vector_de_enlace` asserts the observable platform behaviour instead of skipping and pretending coverage

The teardown has redundant safety nets on this git (2.55.0): `git worktree remove --force` with an absolute path already removes the tree AND the `.git/worktrees/` entry, both for a present tree and for a ghost whose directory vanished. `prune` and the trailing `rmtree` are therefore defence-in-depth whose observable effect is nil today; they are kept, but credited to nobody

`git worktree add <path> HEAD` already detaches on its own (HEAD is a commit-ish), so `--detach` is redundant whenever HEAD is passed; the dangerous form is `git worktree add <path>` with no commit-ish, which creates a branch named after the directory and registers it in the user's repo

A mutation is only valid if it describes a failure the code can actually commit: three F7 mutations targeted redundant lines and passed green with and without them. They were rewritten to attack observable behaviour, not counted as caught

A pytest timeout used to be recorded as `cazada`, which is a false positive: no test ran and failed. `_run_pytest` now returns None on timeout and the verdict is NO CONCLUYENTE; LIMITE_PYTEST was raised 300 -> 600 s because the mutated suite is slower than the base one
rules: Keep LangGraph
Keep RunState typed
LLM proposes; deterministic code validates
No direct Coder writes to main workspace
No shell=True with LLM-generated commands
No MCP/Graphify before M2 E2E
No exposure beyond localhost before auth
New Budget fields enter with defaults; only removal/rename bumps schema version
A passing test proves nothing until a mutation makes it fail
No agent imports a provider SDK; all go through ModelGateway
Only models/providers/ may know about a concrete provider
The standard suite must pass without internet, credentials or an external provider
F3: only `interpret` may talk to the gateway; the deterministic classifier is the permanent fallback
F3: a model failure degrades to the fallback and leaves a recoverable error; it is never silent
F3: the interpreter's scope comes from the user, never from the model
F4: the plan is data, not topology; edges are written by hand and never generated from the plan
F4: the plan always passes through the RunPlan contract; model_construct is never used
F4: a model failure degrades to a deterministic plan and leaves a recoverable error; it is never silent
F4: a plan can never promise more review cycles than the run budget allows
F5: plan_index is the single source of truth for progress; it lives in RunState, not duplicated elsewhere
F5: the executor node advances plan_index; the router only reads it, never calculates
F5: evidence accumulates immutably; no executor overwrites the output of a previous subtask
F5: when the plan is exhausted, execution finalizes; the static M1 route does not apply
F6: the model proposes content; the code derives diff, line counts and hashes -the model never supplies a hash
F6: CodeProposal is what the model generates and CodeChange is what the system derives; they are different contracts on purpose
F6: a `delete` carries no new_content and a `create`/`modify` requires it; the contract rejects the incoherence at the boundary
F6: exceeding Scope limits trims and declares (SCOPE_TRIMMED); it never truncates silently and never discards the whole change
F6: a model failure degrades to a controlled EMPTY change with a recoverable error; inventing a patch is forbidden
F6: the Coder never writes to disk; it only fills RunState.outputs.coder_output (F7 applies the patch)
F6: a model failure must APPEND its error to the existing ones; it must never overwrite the errors of earlier phases
F7: the Coder proposes, the sandbox applies; the Coder never writes to disk and never to the user repo
F7: every write inside the sandbox passes confinement before any effect - never once at the start, always per file
F7: confinement is four barriers (syntax, declared scope, policy, physical root check); any one of them denies
F7: a denied path is recorded and skipped; the remaining legitimate files of the same change still apply
F7: the sandbox is a git worktree, created detached, under a gitignored workspace root, and teardown removes AND prunes
F7: the diff is a real unified diff when the previous content is available; without it, the degradation is declared, never silent
F7: the Coder cannot delete files; destructiveness requires approval and the Supervisor role

F7: the fourth barrier is tested by injecting the resolution outcome, not by planting a symlink: the platform cannot produce a symlink that resolution follows, and a link the system does not resolve proves nothing about the code that judges the resolved path
F7: a mutation must describe a failure the code can commit; a mutation over a redundant line passes green with and without it and verifies nothing
F7: a pytest timeout is NOT a caught mutation -no test failed-; it is reported as non-conclusive, never silently counted as caught
F7: redundancy in the teardown is proven against the filesystem, not assumed; `prune`/`rmtree` are kept as defence in depth but are not credited as the mechanism
F8: a test target is not a command; the id is resolved through a closed in-code table and passed to subprocess as an argument list with shell=False
F8: tests run inside the sandbox worktree, never in the user repo, and the child's PYTHONPATH points at the sandbox src/ so the evidence describes the code that will be approved
F8: a red test is evidence for the Reviewer, not a system error; a timeout is evidence of a hang, not an exception
F8: a sandbox failure becomes a typed RunError and the run ends in needs_human, never a LangGraph traceback
F8: a branch that never executes looks covered; the `fallos` branch was unreachable because a raw OSError escaped before reaching it -writing the test found a defect, not just a blind spot
F8: conditional edges do not appear in get_graph().edges; assert topology on the uncompiled StateGraph (nodes + branches) and by exercising the routers
F9: the model judges, the code decides - the reviewer's verdict is a proposal; three deterministic guards turn it into a decision
F9: a failing TestRun invalidates any ACCEPT the model emits (REGLA 1); the model may disagree with the code, not overrule it on this
F9: exhausting max_review_cycles turns REQUEST_CHANGES into ESCALATE (REGLA 2); the limit lives in the node, not the router, so there is a single source of truth
F9: guard order matters - the test veto runs before the cycle limit, so a vetoed ACCEPT still passes through the limit instead of slipping past it
F9: the deterministic reviewer is the fallback when the model fails (REGLA 3) and it declares itself as such; a fallback that does not say so is indistinguishable from a success
F9: `ProjectRequirements` does not exist as a contract; the requirements are `Instruction` + `TaskInterpretation`, and no parallel duplicate type was invented
F9: `review_cycles_used` advances only on REQUEST_CHANGES; an ACCEPT or an ESCALATE does not consume a cycle
M2: the confirmation of the interpretation is a human act -`TaskInterpretation.confirmed_by_user` is excluded from the JSON schema sent to the model, so the system cannot confirm itself
M2: two human gates, two states, two moments -requirements are confirmed before planning, the change is approved after testing; merging them would leave a client unable to tell what it is being asked
M2: a rejected or unrecognised resumption never confirms and never plans; the failure direction matters, because a client error must not confirm on the human's behalf
M2: the requirements gate is skipped for out-of-scope instructions -asking a human to confirm requirements the system is going to refuse anyway spends a human decision on something already decided
M2: a write before `interrupt()` is lost, because the node re-runs on resume; the awaiting state must be set by the **previous** node (verified by experiment before designing the gate)
M2: `MET-13` must treat a human wait as legitimate -`RunStatus.is_awaiting_human` covers both gates, or a paused run is forced to needs_human as if the topology were broken

F10: a project is a repository **validated at registration**, not a loose path per request; the check is shared with the sandbox (`sandbox.validar_repositorio`) so there is one definition of a usable repo
F10: the node name is a **type**, not a datum -`requirements.completed` etc. allow an exhaustive client switch; the legacy `run.step` is kept while the current frontend listens to it
F10: `coder.completed`, not `coder.started` -the engine reads `stream_mode=updates`, which delivers a node **after** it finishes; naming that event `started` would misdate it
F10: a human wait is not an outcome -`_persistir` runs when the graph pauses, so `run.completed`/`run.failed` are emitted only for terminal states
F10: the outcome event goes **immediately before** `run.done`, which is what closes the SSE stream; anything written after can fall in the next batch and be lost
F10: every event is redacted at `append_event`, the single point all events pass through; the logging filter does not cover this path

F10: a domain exception that escapes unmapped reaches the client as a 500 with a traceback -typed handlers give 4xx with `error_class`; a `TypeError` is deliberately **not** mapped, so a server defect cannot masquerade as a client error

F10: `PolicyViolationError` does not exist in this repository -the Policy Engine returns `PolicyEffect.DENY` and a denial travels as a typed `RunError` inside the run; no type was invented that nothing raises
F10: the server binds to 127.0.0.1 as a **constant**, not an argument; with no auth (AUD-06) exposing it would publish the ability to run code, and a flag invites opening it `just to test`
F10: the SSE payload is the whole `RunEvent` envelope (`seq`/`at`/`kind`/`data`), not the bare payload -the envelope is what lets a client order and dedupe by `seq`

F10: reading a run's full event history **through SSE** is unreliable -the stream closes at the first `run.done` in the batch, and between human pauses the run is not terminal so the stream does not close until `timeout_s`. Read legs over SSE to prove delivery; read the record to assert the sequence

mutations.f7: 12/12 (after fixing 4 uncaught mutations and a false-positive timeout verdict)
mutations.f8: 9/9 (4 blind spots found on the first pass — shell=True at the call site, PYTHONPATH, the `fallos` branch, the coder router — and closed with real tests; the `fallos` blind spot uncovered a real defect: a raw OSError escaped Sandbox.escribir and reached LangGraph as a traceback)
mutations.f9: 8/8 — the test veto (REGLA 1), the cycle limit (REGLA 2), the guard order, the declared fallback (REGLA 3), the reviewer model wiring, the cycle accounting, the ACCEPT route and the test evidence in the context
mutations.m2: 7/7 — the requirements gate being skipped, the awaiting state not being marked, the confirmation not being recorded, a rejection planning anyway, human modifications being discarded, an unrecognised resumption being treated as approved, and the MET-13 safety net confusing a wait with a hang
mutations.f10: 13/13 — events stored unredacted, a human pause emitted as run.failed, the outcome event not emitted, the human wait announced with the wrong gate's event, the per-node milestones not emitted, the engine stringifying a corrections resumption, project registration skipping repo validation, the project path not overriding the request's, SandboxError mapped to 500 instead of 422, the server listening on all interfaces, the resumption not reserving the right (two concurrent requests both winning), `confirm-requirements` accepting the approval gate, and `approve` accepting the requirements gate. The last three were added this phase; a `shutdown` mutation that had been counted earlier was retracted after proving it attacked a redundant line (the original `shutdown(wait=True)` already waits), and the underlying regression test was removed with it. RE-RUN DURING F11 (after AUD-11 retired `run.awaiting_approval`): 12/13 — the same run reported `la reanudacion no reserva el derecho` as NOT caught. That mutant removes the claim that makes `reclamar_reanudacion` atomic; the test that should catch it (`test_dos_confirmaciones_concurrentes_solo_reanudan_una_vez`) drives two threads through a barrier and asserts `sorted(codigos) == [200, 409]`, so it only observes the race when the worker thread has not yet finished the first resume. The verdict is therefore timing-dependent, and the guard is weaker than a 13/13 count implies. The mutant was retargeted in the same phase for AUD-11 (`run.awaiting_approval` no longer exists, so the old pattern could not apply).
mutations.f12: 8/8 (this run: baseline green, every mutant caught, tree restored green) — promoting over an unauthorised repository, promoting a patch that changed after review (integrity), a path outside `allowed_paths`, a protected path, the sandbox not being torn down on finalize, a rejection marked as `completed`, requesting changes not spending a review cycle, and the human's comments not reaching the state. blockers_and_debt.title: Test Runner (F8) absent
blockers_and_debt.detail: The M2 DoD could not close without it: no test evidence means the reviewer has nothing to judge.
blockers_and_debt.how_to_close: Implemented in F8 (commit f1ced97): tools/runner.py runs only the allowed targets inside the sandbox and records real TestRun evidence (exit code, stdout/stderr, duration, argv).

blockers_and_debt.title: The sandbox is not wired into the graph
blockers_and_debt.detail: F7 proved isolation in tests, but no run applied a patch.
blockers_and_debt.how_to_close: M3 done in F8: the `apply_sandbox` node sits between coder and run_tests (coder -> apply_sandbox -> run_tests -> reviewer).

blockers_and_debt.title: No authentication on the API
blockers_and_debt.detail: Open finding from the external audit; mitigated only by localhost-only exposure.
blockers_and_debt.how_to_close: Auth before any exposure beyond localhost (project rule).

blockers_and_debt.title: Frontend verification is a separate harness
blockers_and_debt.detail: tools/verify_frontend.py is not part of the pytest suite, and there is no CSS/jsdom coverage.
blockers_and_debt.how_to_close: Fold the frontend checks into the standard suite, or declare the gap explicitly.

blockers_and_debt.title: Docs naming differs from the Arquitecto's expectation
blockers_and_debt.detail: The requested 00-PROJECT-BRIEF.md / 01-ARCHITECTURE.md / 02-CONTRACTS.md / 03-SECURITY.md / 04-ROADMAP.md / 05-DECISIONS.md / 06-EVALUATION.md do NOT exist. The real docs are 01-arquitectura.md .. 06-contrato-frontend-backend.md plus auditoria-2026-10-06/00..13 and BASELINE-*.md. There are NO ADRs (decisions live as DEC-xx in 01-arquitectura.md).
blockers_and_debt.how_to_close: Resolved with an index layer: docs/00-PROJECT-BRIEF.md .. 06-EVALUATION.md were added as aliases pointing to the canonical documents, and DEC-01..DEC-11 were extracted into docs/05-DECISIONS.md (plus DEC-12..DEC-17 for the M2 phase decisions).

blockers_and_debt.title: The Reviewer is deterministic, not model-driven
blockers_and_debt.detail: The reviewer read the TestRun exit_code and returned a verdict from it: a traffic light, not a review. DoD item 9 (requirements + change + tests) could not be met by a node that never saw the requirements.
blockers_and_debt.how_to_close: F9: the reviewer calls the ModelGateway with ReviewVerdict, sending the requirements (Instruction + TaskInterpretation), the current subtask, the CodeProposal diff and the real TestRun evidence, with three deterministic guards on top (test veto, cycle limit, declared fallback).

blockers_and_debt.title: No human confirmation of the interpreted requirements (DoD item 3)
blockers_and_debt.detail: HITL existed only at the approval gate, after the work was done. The system could plan and build on a misreading of the request without anyone confirming the reading first.
blockers_and_debt.how_to_close: M2: `confirm_requirements_gate` between `interpret` and `plan`, with `AWAITING_HUMAN_REQUIREMENTS_CONFIRMATION`. The human can confirm or correct the interpretation; a rejection escalates without planning.

blockers_and_debt.title: Legacy SSE event names kept for the current frontend
blockers_and_debt.detail: F10 added the canonical event set (`requirements.completed`, `plan.completed`, `coder.completed`, `tests.completed`, `run.awaiting_human`, `run.completed`, `run.failed`) but kept `run.created`, `run.step`, `run.status`, `run.awaiting_approval`, `run.report`, `run.error` and `run.done` emitting, because `frontend/index.html` listened for the legacy names. Retiring them would have broken an interface that was not part of F10.
blockers_and_debt.how_to_close: F11 retired `run.step`, `run.status`, `run.report`, `run.error` and `run.awaiting_approval` at the source (`contracts/api.py`), in the engine (`_ejecutar`, `_persistir`, `abortar`), in the orphan-run recovery path (`state/store.py`) and in the mutation harness, and regenerated `frontend/contracts.json`. `run.created`, `run.started` and `run.done` are kept -they have no canonical substitute, and `run.done` is the signal that closes each SSE leg, not an alias of anything. The new frontend consumes only the canonical set, and `tools/verify_frontend.py` asserts that no legacy name is consumed.

blockers_and_debt.title: Two defects in the resume path found only by driving the API
blockers_and_debt.detail: (1) `RunEngine.resume` stringified any non-`ApprovalDecision` value, so a dict of requirement corrections became an unrecognisable string and the gate read it as a rejection: the corrections path never worked through the engine. (2) `_persistir` emitted `run.failed` on every non-`COMPLETED` state, including a human pause. Both were invisible to the M2 tests, which call `app.invoke(Command(resume=...))` directly and bypass `RunEngine.resume`.
blockers_and_debt.how_to_close: Fixed in F10 with tests in tests/test_f10_api.py that drive the same path the HTTP client uses. The lesson is recorded: a path only the API takes must be tested through the API.

blockers_and_debt.title: Stale phase label in the prototype frontend
blockers_and_debt.detail: `/health` reported `fase: "M1"` until F10, when it was corrected to "M3" (it was simply wrong). Two static strings in `frontend/index.html` still said "fase M1" (the descriptive paragraph and the STT note). The health **chip** is rendered from the API, so it already showed the correct phase -the page was therefore internally inconsistent.
blockers_and_debt.how_to_close: F11 replaced `frontend/index.html` entirely: it is now the Vite source entry point and carries no phase string at all -the phase is read from `/health` and rendered by React. `tools/verify_frontend.py` asserts that no stale milestone label survives in the built page (`MENCIONA_M1=false`).
